Numerical aperture (NA) is a measure of the ability of a lens or other optical system to focus light into or out of it. It is defined as the ratio of the lens's focal length to its diameter. In other words, NA is the number of times that the lens or system can bend the light path before it reaches the edge of the lens or system.

For example, a lens with a NA of 0.5 would focus the light into a circular beam with a diameter of 0.5mm, while a lens with a NA of 0.1 would focus the light into a circular beam with a diameter of 1mm.

NA is important in optics because it determines the amount of light that can be collected or focused by the lens or system. Lenses with higher NA are more efficient at collecting and focusing light, while lenses with lower NA are more diffuse and scatter less light. In addition, NA is also used to determine the resolution of an optical system, as a higher NA will allow for a smaller spot size on the target.
